props.gloss_en: the mishna: a live eight-month-born -- its slaughter does not purify it, since there is no slaughter for its kind
the mishna: 'one that was born a tereifa from the womb -- from where?' [said of an animal that never had a time of fitness]
the slaughter of a tereifa renders it pure [from carcass impurity]
the baraita: let the live eight-month-born prove it -- for there IS slaughter for its kind
the baraita: [yet] its slaughter does not purify it
Rav Kahana: there is slaughter for its kind -- by virtue of its mother
Rav Kahana: and our tanna does not refute from its mother's kind
the verse says 'and if [some] of the animal dies' (Lev 11:39) -- some of the animal imparts impurity and some does not; and which is that? a tereifa that one slaughtered
side A: one who put his hand into the womb and slaughtered a live nine-month fetus -- that slaughter permits it
side B: that slaughter inside the womb does not permit it
per R' Meir: he said a ben pekua requires slaughter only where it emerged into the air of the world; inside its mother, slaughter does not permit it
or perhaps even per the Rabbis, the Merciful One made four simanim fit for it

questions.gloss_en: Rav Hoshaya: one put his hand into the animal's womb and slaughtered a live nine-month fetus -- what is the law? Rav Chananya's proof is deflected; the text records no resolution and no teiku

supports.gloss_en: ולהאי תנא דפריך ... מנא ליה? נפקא ליה מדרב יהודה אמר רב (ואמרי לה במתניתא תנא): וכי ימות מן הבהמה -- זו טרפה ששחטה
תא שמע: הרי שנולדה טרפה מן הבטן -- ואי איתא, משכחת לה דהיתה לה שעת הכושר, דאי בעי עייל ידיה ושחטה

deflected_by.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבא: תני שנוצרה טרפה מן הבטן, ומשכחת לה בבעלת חמש רגלים -- read 'formed a tereifa', as with one that has five legs; it never had a time of fitness

objections.gloss_en: והתניא: בן שמנה חי יוכיח, שאף על פי שיש במינו שחיטה אין שחיטתו מטהרתו -- but a baraita says there IS slaughter for its kind

answered_by.gloss_en: יש במינו שחיטה אגב אמו, ותנא דידן מינא דאמיה לא פריך -- the baraita means slaughter by virtue of its mother, and our tanna does not refute from its mother's kind
